knownDifferences: Identifiers are lowercase snake_case (for example CreatedAt becomes created_at; User_Id becomes user_id); foreign key and index names are renamed too. Data values are never lowercased.

datetime columns become TIMESTAMP without time zone and keep the source values exactly; it is not known whether the legacy application stored UTC or local times (only LockoutEndDateUtc is UTC by name), so no zone conversion is made.

SQL Server compared text case-insensitively; PostgreSQL is case-sensitive. Username uniqueness is enforced case-insensitively by a partial unique index on lower(name) where deleted_at IS NULL, so authentication must compare lower(name) = lower(input). Role names use a plain case-sensitive unique index.
bit columns become BOOLEAN; the identity columns become GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY and the data supplies explicit ids (the sequences are reset after the load).
Index names that were duplicated across tables in SQL Server (for example IX_UserId) were prefixed with the table name, then renamed to snake_case.
